trust_decision.summary: The server-side message filter decides whether a received message id is one this role may receive; at the pinned commit it refuses only SERVICE_ACCEPT as server-to-client-only, so ids 31 (KEXDH_REPLY / GEX_GROUP / ECDH / KEM reply alias) and 33 (GEX_REPLY) from the client reach client-role handlers whenever no expectMsgId is pending.

landing_point.why: The summary names the GEX group message and primality test, so a reader goes to DoKexDhGexGroup / ValidateKexDhGexGroup (mp_prime_is_prime_ex at src/internal.c:8654 and 8671) or to the dispatch case at src/internal.c:13137-13147.

fix_sites.entry_point: wolfSSH_accept() / wolfSSH_worker() / any server read driving DoReceive -> DoPacket -> IsMessageAllowed(ssh, msg, WS_MSG_RECV) (src/internal.c:13044)
fix_sites.module_kind: core protocol state machine (message-id role/state filter)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the client-side mirror (src/internal.c:827): the advisory concerns an unauthenticated client attacking a server; a client talks only to a server it chose, and the report names only messages 31 and 33 received by the server.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The server must still accept the client's own KEX messages in the same state: KEXDH_GEX_REQUEST (34), KEXDH_INIT/KEXECDH_INIT/KEXKEM_INIT (30) and GEX_INIT (32), all sharing the transport KEX range 30-49 with the blocked ids; blocking the whole KEX range or all of id 31's neighbours, or adding a check keyed on kexId, breaks normal DH, ECDH, KEM and GEX handshakes and rekeys. The client must keep receiving 31/33 (same filter function family).

O6_input_shapes: id 31 with any other kexId (DH / ECDH / KEM reply alias) -> DoKexDhReply (src/internal.c:13149-13152; aliases at wolfssh/internal.h:1812-1816)
initial pre-auth KEX (acceptState < ACCEPT_KEYED) and rekey on an established session (acceptState past keyed), both with expectMsgId == MSGID_NONE (fix.diff:885-900)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client-side filter refuses only SERVICE_REQUEST and USERAUTH_REQUEST as client-only; KEXDH_INIT (30), GEX_INIT (32) and GEX_REQUEST (34) from a server reach server-role handlers DoKexDhInit / DoKexDhGexRequest -> SendKexDhGexGroup when no expectMsgId is pending.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Opposite direction: the advisory is about a pre-auth client attacking a server; a malicious server is a different threat model, and the published fix did not touch the client filter.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 120 lines below the fix site (src/internal.c:824-938 vs 702)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second dispatcher or rekey fast path that switches on kexId for id 31 without going through IsMessageAllowed, e.g. a strict-KEX first-packet handler.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Id 31 is overloaded across four meanings chosen by kexId, and the project keeps adding KEX paths (strict KEX, ML-KEM), so a maintainer could plausibly add a handler that dispatches on kexId before the role filter runs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A side check placed inside a handler (for example DoKexDhGexRequest gated on ctx->side) rather than in the filter, with the mirror handler left ungated.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handlers already carry per-message defensive logic (SkipGuessedKexMsg at src/internal.c:8527, 8710), so per-handler guards are idiomatic here.

O9_family: protocol state machine / role confusion: message-id acceptance by endpoint role (CWE-372), with a pre-auth CPU-cost consequence (Miller-Rabin on an attacker-chosen group)

O10_build.toolchain: autotools (autogen.sh, configure, make) against a wolfSSL built with --enable-wolfssh
O10_build.project_tests: tests/regress.c (message-filter tests via wolfSSH_TestIsMessageAllowed, src/internal.c:23999; TestServerOnlyUserauthMsgsBlocked at tests/regress.c:2510); tests/unit.c GEX group/request tests (tests/unit.c:2568-3232)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject id 31 only inside the pre-keyed block (src/internal.c:783-787), or add a side check inside DoKexDhGexGroup only; either leaves the rekey window open, or leaves id 31 under non-GEX kexIds and id 33 reaching DoKexDhReply.

out_of_scope_notes: Server-side ordering inside GEX (for example KEXDH_INIT 30 or GEX_INIT 32 arriving before GEX_REQUEST 34 while expectMsgId is NONE) is a state-order question, not role confusion; not pursued.
